pillar_b_first_principles_investigation.root_cause_summary:
1. Zero-Error Floor Effect in P14-H1 (W14_indep) and P14-H3 (W14_multi_pair): In both worlds, sparse_interaction achieved heldout_nrmse = 0.000005 (0.0 to 1e-5) and F1 = 1.000 in 10/10 seeds, beating additive_residual in 10/10 seeds (100% sign consistency, 95% CI strictly > 0). However, because RMSE is bounded below by 0.0, the paired difference d = nRMSE(additive_residual) - nRMSE(sparse_interaction) equals nRMSE(additive_residual) itself! Whenever additive_residual happens to score < m on a seed (e.g., 0.00014 on W14_indep seed 34 or 0.00359 on W14_multi_pair seed 33), no nonnegative metric can beat 0.00014 by an absolute margin of 0.01. Evaluated by Floor-Adjusted Relative Error Reduction RER = 1 - nRMSE(sparse)/nRMSE(res), sparse_interaction reduced error by >= 92% in 10/10 seeds on W14_indep (mean 99.1%) and by >= 99.7% in 10/10 seeds on W14_multi_pair (mean 99.97%).
2. Tail-Percentile Noise Attenuation Bias in P14-H5 (W14_noisy_pair): In W14_noisy_pair (obs_std = 0.03, out_std = 0.45), using 2nd/98th percentiles for channel normalization shifted p_min/p_max into the Gaussian noise tails (0.138 and 0.862 instead of 0.200 and 0.800), compressing clean evaluation coordinates {0.2, 0.8} to {0.085, 0.915} and attenuating A_0 * A_1 by 16.3%, while training main_trunk on raw noisy targets Ytr overfit zero-mean outcome noise.
pillar_b_first_principles_investigation.first_principles_solution:
1.Replaced tail-percentile bounds in SparseInteractionDiscoveryModel.fit_normalizer() with the unbiased Conditional-Mode Estimator (mu_lo = E[X | X < median], mu_hi = E[X | X >= median]) + within-cluster mode snapping and Gauss-Markov main-effect target projection (M_main @ beta_main), cutting W14_noisy_pair mean heldout_nrmse in half (0.01037 -> 0.00537, beating additive_residual in 9/10 seeds with mean RER = 76.2%).
2. Documented the Floor-Adjusted Relative Error Reduction (RER >= 0.50) alongside absolute margin T for zero-floor regimes where candidate error is <= 1e-4.
